page: The Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration exposes 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). It provides 32.0 GB of memory, equating to an allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The virtual machine does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options such as Azure Premium Storage. It also does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,146.0 falling into the top quartile. However, due to its constrained physical footprint of a single core, multi-threaded metrics scale lower; stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests rank in the bottom tiers. Large-block uncached memory operations register at 21.51 GB/sec for reads and 14.37 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks reflect 2.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

With its 16:1 memory-to-core ratio, the E4-2s_v6 provides a cost-efficient resource density for applications requiring significant memory footprints without paying for excess compute cores. It is suitable for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and enterprise applications constrained by per-core software licensing.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core with hyperthreading. The VM is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache and advanced vector sets including AVX-512 and AMX. There is no bundled local storage, integrated GPU accelerator, or complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2,146.0, though overall multi-threaded throughput is naturally limited by the single-core configuration. Large-block uncached memory throughput reaches 21.51 GB/sec read and 14.37 GB/sec write. This profile is well suited for memory-bound workloads such as in-memory caches, memory-intensive staging databases, and software environments subject to core-based licensing costs.
